subject: pcount:  observed count as a covariate of detection

messages.author: e394633264e35c35
messages.subject: pcount:  observed count as a covariate of detection
parts:
I have an over dispersed pcount ZIP model for beetle count data that were collected using baited traps (257 sites x 3 observation periods per site).  I suspect the overdispersion (c-hat = 3.6) is due to pheromone being released by trapped beetles which attracts other beetles at a greater rate than bait alone.  So, in essence, I think the observed count data for an observation period should be included as a detection covariate.  Ecologically, this seems appealing, but is this statistically appropriate?

Thanks,
Doug

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] pcount:  observed count as a covariate of detection
parts:
Dear Doug,

 

you want a model where p depends on N or on lambda. I agree that such a model may make sense ecologically under some situations. Also, for birds, for instance, it’s quite possible that individuals sing more when they occur at higher density. Such a model cannot be fitted in unmarked.

 

A while ago I experimented with such a model of density-dependent detection and fitted it in BUGS. Things seemed to work well for simulated data but when I applied it to real data, I got some nonsensical results and then gave up.

 

At any case, if you want to pursue this idea you would very probably have to move to BUGS.

 

Kind regards  --- Marc

Doug,

Though the application (within-season movement) and model (dynamic occupancy) were different than yours, you might see how Betts et al. 2008 (http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.0906-7590.2008.05490.x/abstract) included observed abundance as a covariate.

- Giancarlo
